gloss: question (on a test or survey); query; problem (set for answering)

definitions.gloss: question (on a test or survey); query; problem (set for answering)
definitions.explanation: A question that has been deliberately composed and presented for someone to answer, typically on an examination, questionnaire, or survey. More formal than 質問 and implies intentional design.

examples.japanese: {設問|せつもん}に{答|こた}えなさい。
アンケートの{設問|せつもん}は{全部|ぜんぶ}で{十問|じゅうもん}ある。
examples.english: There are ten questions in total on the survey.

examples.japanese: {設問|せつもん}の{意図|いと}を{正|ただ}しく{読|よ}み{取|と}ることが、{試験|しけん}で{良|よ}い{点|てん}を{取|と}る{鍵|かぎ}だ。
examples.english: Correctly understanding the intent of the question is the key to getting good marks on an exam.

notes:
A formal word for a question that has been deliberately set or posed, typically on an exam, questionnaire, or survey. Composed of {設|せつ} (to set up, establish) and {問|もん} (question). More formal than {質問|しつもん} and implies the question was purposefully designed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {設問|せつもん}に{答|こた}える: to answer a question
- {設問|せつもん}を{設|もう}ける: to set up questions
- {設問|せつもん}の{意図|いと}: the intent of the question
- {設問|せつもん}{形式|けいしき}: question format

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {質問|しつもん} — question (general, can be asked verbally)
- {問題|もんだい} — problem; question (broader, includes exam questions and issues)
- {出題|しゅつだい} — setting questions; question composition (the act of creating questions)
- {問|とい} — question; inquiry (more literary or used in test instructions)
